A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VisionReasoner and provide readable text, equations, tables and figures. v1 ends with references; v4 includes Appendices A–H. Retained material can be matched reliably across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original detection, segmentation, counting and VQA evaluations, together with reward, training-data, sampling and reasoning ablations.

after.justification: v4 retains these experiments and adds human reasoning evaluations, an RL algorithm comparison, expression-level grounding results and TaskRouter evaluation.

M1.justification: Appendix C adds a separately GRPO-trained TaskRouter for automatically identifying the requested task, supplementing v1's user-specified task category. Appendix F describes pose/depth output-module extensions. These are auxiliary extensions; the central perception architecture, reward components and Hungarian matching remain unchanged. Expanded reward specifications and pseudocode do not establish changes to the original procedure.

E1.justification: The original perception benchmarks and VQA coverage are retained. Appendix C adds a distinct text-only task-classification dataset and task, while Figure 10 demonstrates referring-expression pose and depth estimation. This expands the represented task requirements beyond the original evaluations. Expression-level grounding reuses existing coverage, and Appendix H's taxonomy is not evidence of additional evaluated tasks.

E2.justification: The main perception baseline sets remain unchanged. Supporting comparisons add DAPO against GRPO, DINO-X alongside YOLO-World in Figure 2, and Qwen2.5-1.5B against TaskRouter in Table 11. The permutation-matching comparator from v1 Table 5 is removed from v4 Table 3.

E3.justification: v4 adds human assessment of 200 ReasonSeg-val traces using image/answer consistency and IoU strata, expression-level RefCOCO(+/g) evaluation alongside retained instance-level results, and a GRPO/DAPO comparison trained on 2,000 RefCOCOg samples. TaskRouter introduces a 1.5B-model evaluation with 20,000 training and 4,000 test instructions. These substantially expand evaluation design without replacing the original benchmark protocols.

E4.justification: v4 adds an optimizer-choice ablation and a human analysis connecting reasoning consistency with localization quality. Figure 2 supplies a comparative complex-query case study, and appendix qualitative examples are expanded. Existing reward, sampling, reasoning and training-data ablations remain; the matching-efficiency analysis drops the permutation comparison and focuses on batching.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests or comparable uncertainty estimates. The new human-evaluation sample counts and consistency percentages describe evaluation design and outcomes, without introducing uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Main perception and VQA scores are retained. v4 adds GRPO/DAPO ReasonSeg-val scores of 61.9/61.7, human image/answer consistency of 97.0%/90.5%, TaskRouter/Qwen2.5-1.5B accuracy of 99.1%/46.3%, and expression-level grounding results. The matching-speed claim changes from 6 × 10^35 to 4× by removing the permutation comparator; the retained Hungarian timings are unchanged.

T1.justification: The existing perception/output equations and reward reasoning are retained. The added GRPO equations and matching pseudocode explain the already-described optimization and assignment procedures; the router equation specifies its input-output mapping. Neither version introduces substantive theoretical results, proofs or formal assumptions, and the terminology/taxonomy additions are conceptual clarification.

C1.justification: The unified perception contribution, ten-benchmark claim and headline relative gains remain unchanged. v4 adds an explicit claim in the abstract, introduction and conclusion that human evaluation establishes faithful, reliable reasoning despite training without annotated reasoning traces. This strengthens the claimed quality of the existing reasoning capability.

C2.justification: v4 interprets human consistency ratings as evidence of faithful reasoning and GRPO/DAPO results as evidence of training stability and generalizability. It adds applicability discussion contrasting complex instructions with categorical queries and proposes hybrid deployment. The earlier suggestion of potentially solving 10% of vision task types is replaced by a broader taxonomy explicitly qualified as evaluated on only ten representative tasks.

D1.justification: v4 supplies exact format-reward values, joint matching pseudocode, the training/inference prompt, explicit Qwen2.5-VL/SAM2 initialization, and TaskRouter data-generation and training information. These materially improve implementation documentation without establishing changes to existing settings. Conversely, v1's six-hour training-time disclosure is removed. The repository access link remains unchanged.

R1.justification: v4 adds DINO-X, DAPO, the Qwen2.5 language-model report and ChatGPT references, while removing OpenAI o1 and Papers with Code. It expands positioning against traditional detectors and removes some explicit Seg-Zero dependency statements from the method description, while retaining Seg-Zero elsewhere. The overall positioning around unified RL-based visual perception remains stable.

P1.justification: v4 substantially reorganizes the narrative: it inserts method preliminaries, rewrites model/reward explanations, consolidates experimental settings, and moves benchmark details and much qualitative discussion into appendices. It also introduces terminology clarification and changes the title and citation style. This is substantial restructuring beyond the added experiments alone.

P2.justification: Benchmark statistics and examples move to Appendix A. The original qualitative figure becomes a compact main-text display plus an expanded appendix figure. v4 adds detector-comparison and pose/depth figures, experimental and explanatory tables, and a pseudocode display. Table arrangements, captions, running headers and document typography also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v4 improves reproducibility through matching pseudocode and the exact prompt, clarifies instance-versus-expression evaluation, and replaces the astronomical permutation-based speed comparison with a useful 4× batching comparison. Human assessment and optimizer comparisons add relevant evidence. However, the human study omits rater and agreement details, and consistency ratings support a narrower conclusion than the new faithfulness claims suggest. The net improvement is useful but limited.
